title: A workspace with shared dependencies
summary: Split the build into member crates that inherit versions and profiles from the workspace.

scenario.briefing: The campus CLI and its core library now live in separate crates, but each one pins serde separately and the release profile differs. Create a workspace that shares dependency versions and release settings.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: List both crate directories in workspace.members.
Keep one serde and serde_json requirement under workspace.dependencies.
Members use serde.workspace = true instead of repeating a version.
Declare [profile.release] once at the root; member profile sections are ignored.

misconceptions.testDescription: Dependency versions live once in the workspace.
misconceptions.feedback: Two pins drift apart and the workspace builds against different major versions in one dependency graph. Declare the version once and inherit it.

misconceptions.diagnostic: Approving reqwest = "*" because Cargo resolves conflicts automatically.
misconceptions.feedback: A wildcard cannot prevent conflicts; it removes the constraint that would surface them. State a compatible range and let the shared lockfile pin the resolution.

sections.title: One manifest owns shared versions
sections.body: A workspace root lists member directories, and workspace.dependencies declares versions once. A member then writes serde.workspace = true, which pulls the version and features from the root instead of restating them.

sections.title: Profiles apply to the whole build
sections.body: Profiles are defined at the workspace root and apply to every member. Shared metadata under workspace.package lets members inherit fields like edition and license with field.workspace = true.

vocabulary.definition: A set of crates that share one lockfile, target directory, and dependency resolution.
A version requirement declared once under [workspace.dependencies] and inherited by members.
A named set of compiler and linker settings, such as release, declared at the workspace root.

steps.title: Declare a Cargo workspace
steps.prompt: Edit the root Cargo.toml. Add the workspace members, move serde and serde_json into workspace.dependencies, and set a shared release profile. Member crates inherit with workspace = true.

files.content:
[workspace]
members = ["crates/core"]

[workspace.dependencies]
serde = "1.0.203"
serde_json = "1.0.117"

[profile.release]
lto = "thin"

steps.title: Review the workspace manifest
steps.prompt: Review the workspace files and select every real problem.

artifact.title: Cargo.toml and members
artifact.caption: The members pin serde separately and the CLI pulls an HTTP client with a wildcard.
artifact.content:
[workspace]
members = ["crates/core", "crates/cli"]

[workspace.dependencies]
serde = { version = "1.0.203", features = ["derive"] }

[profile.release]
lto = "thin"

# crates/core/Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "campus-core"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
serde = { version = "1.0.199", features = ["derive"] }

# crates/cli/Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "campus-cli"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
campus-core = { path = "../core" }
serde = { version = "1.0.203", features = ["derive"] }
reqwest = "*"

findings.label: campus-core pins serde 1.0.199 while the workspace declares 1.0.203.
Both members restate serde instead of inheriting with serde.workspace = true.
reqwest = "*" accepts any version and makes resolution unpredictable.
The members already inherit the workspace serde version.

verdicts.label: Block the change until versions are inherited and the wildcard is replaced.
Ship it; Cargo resolves the conflicts automatically.
Only the manifest formatting needs work.

steps.explanation: Versions are declared twice and already disagree, so members can compile against different serde releases. A wildcard adds an unbounded dependency, and a regenerated lockfile can silently move it. Move the versions to workspace.dependencies and inherit them.
hints: Compare the member manifests with the workspace manifest.
A wildcard removes the constraint that would surface a conflict.
Members that restate versions do not inherit the workspace pin.
